where: the 'This deployment' block below the rule: the 'Check again' button at x=256-384, y=401-437, and the 'Checked 6:41 pm' fact it refreshes at x=819-927, y=384 — and the same control pair in kiosk-setup-denied at y=580-616
finding:
'Check again' arrived, but nothing on the page reports back when the answer does not change. The admin's actual loop on this screen is grant the IAM role in another tab, come back, re-check — and IAM takes thirty to a hundred and twenty seconds to propagate, so the first two or three checks are supposed to still say no. In that state the page after a click is pixel-identical to the page before it: same badge, same explanation, same command. The only thing that moves is a 12px timestamp 620px to the right of the button the person just clicked and 35px above it, and they would have had to memorise the old value to notice. So the admin cannot tell 'checked again, still refused' from 'the button did nothing', and the third click is a route reload — which is exactly the thing this button was added to remove. In the healthy frame there is not even a slot for a reply: the markup is `
` and nothing else.
evidence: kiosk-setup--desktop.html SigningCard: the healthy section is heading, badge+caveat row, `dl`, then a bare button — no `aria-live` element anywhere in it. kiosk-setup-denied--desktop.html does carry one, `<span aria-live="polite" class="text-xs text-ink-400">`, but it is inline third in the button row with no reserved width or height, and at 12px ink-400 it would be the smallest, dimmest text in a block whose verdict badge is 11px and whose body copy is 14px ink-300. The `dl` runs `lg:flex-row lg:gap-6` so 'Checked' lands at the far right end of a 671px-wide fact row while the control sits at its left edge. Vertical room is not the constraint: the healthy page ends at y=607 of 900 and no desktop-full frame was even rendered for this scene.
direction: Give the re-check a reply in the place the eye already is — beside or under the button that caused it — and let it state the verdict and the time together ('Still cannot sign kiosk tokens — checked 6:52 pm'), so an unchanged answer still looks like an answer. Reserve its height so nothing below jumps, and use the same element in both states rather than only the failing one. Moving 'Checked' next to the button it belongs to would also stop the freshness of the whole diagnostic living at the opposite end of a fact row.

where: the healthy admin page as a whole: 'Ready to pair' badge and its caveat at y=358, the two small-print paragraphs at y=500-540 and y=567-607, and the empty region x=840-1408 / y=20-300 beside the pairing form
finding: The journey's second job is 'find out why a kiosk that has a code is not signing itself in', and the state most admins will actually meet is this one — the IAM grant is a once-per-deployment problem, so on nearly every Friday the deployment is fine and the lobby screen is still stuck. On that page the only block that addresses the question says 'Ready to pair … It says nothing about the screen in the lobby' and stops. That sentence is honest and must stay, but it leaves the person who came here with a stuck iPad holding a screen that has disclaimed their question and offered no next move. The answers are already on the page and in the journey — the code expires in ten minutes, an iOS home-screen install has its own storage and needs its own second pairing, a kiosk drops when its approver's access is deactivated — but they are scattered as a hint under the button, a line of 12px ink-500 small print framed as 'to retire one', and (the home-screen case) nowhere at all. Nothing is grouped under the question the person arrived with.
evidence: The healthy content ends at y=607 in a 900px viewport and the shoot produced no `--desktop-full` frame for any desktop scene, so nothing is below the fold; the top band right of the form, x≈840 to the column edge at 1408 by y=20-300, is 568×280px of empty column. The two paragraphs that carry the only troubleshooting facts are `text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-500 max-w-prose` — 12px, the dimmest type on the page, at the very bottom of the content — and their first words are '/kiosk is a self-serve screen' and 'A kiosk stays signed in until…', neither of which reads as an answer to 'it is showing a code and nothing happens'. The ten-minute fact lives 250px higher, attached to the form.
direction: Use the width that is already empty: put a short 'the kiosk still isn't signing in' group beside or under the deployment block, holding the three causes that are true and already known — code age, the separate storage an installed-to-home-screen kiosk gets, and a deactivated approver — as a list rather than as prose in three different registers. This is regrouping facts the page already states, not a new claim about the lobby screen, so the 'nothing may claim a kiosk is healthy' rule is untouched; the caveat sentence should stay verbatim as the thing that introduces it.

where: the `pre` holding the gcloud command, x=256-1014, y=518-570, second line beginning '76406@appspot…'
finding: The clipping is fixed — the whole command including 'serviceAccountTokenCreator' is now readable, which closes the round-one blocker on this element. What replaced it is a wrap chosen by the browser rather than by anyone: `break-words` split the line inside the service account identifier, so the command reads '…--member=serviceAccount:tally-' / '76406@appspot.gserviceaccount.com …'. An admin who types this on the machine that actually has gcloud — rarely the one showing this page — has a fair chance of producing 'tally- 76406@…' or dropping the hyphen, and a malformed member is a grant that fails for a reason that looks nothing like the reason they are here for. 'Copy command' beside it is the real mitigation and is now a proper 44px target, but it only helps on the same machine.
evidence: The `pre` is `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words` in a `lg:col-span-2` cell 758px wide; the command is 158 characters at 12px mono (~1141px), so it takes two lines and the break falls at the 79th character, mid-identifier. The right third of the grid is empty at that vertical position — 'Phone search' ends at y≈520 — and the full content column is 1152px, so the block has room to be wider or to break where a person would.
direction: Break the command where a shell would: backslash continuations at argument boundaries, so each line is one whole flag and no identifier is ever split. Same two lines, same height, but a line a person can retype.
